current.text: Experts expect him to open the season as a starter next to Tyler Herro, ahead of Kevin Porter Jr. One expert sees him as at worst the second-best guard on the Bucks.
The Milwaukee backcourt is crowded. Tyler Herro, Kevin Porter Jr., Gary Trent Jr., Braden Burries, Jakucionis, Green and Brandon Boston all compete for guard minutes.

Experts disagree on how safe his role is. Some worry about his minutes next to Herro, Porter and Kuzma and have low confidence in any Bucks player. Others trust new coach Taylor Jenkins to use him well and see his role as fairly set.
He finished around 51st in fantasy last season.
Experts say the ESPN rank around 105 is far too low. He is probably close to top 50 value, and drafting him in the 60s, or as high as pick 50, is fine.
He has top 40 upside, but that depends on how Milwaukee uses him.
One expert calls him probably the best Bucks player to target in drafts, though team uncertainty limits his confidence.
One expert expects him to score about 20 points per game under Taylor Jenkins and says he could lead the team in scoring.
He is 24 and on a very cheap contract. He will be an unrestricted free agent after this season.
Milwaukee may not re-sign him, so experts see him as a trade candidate. A trade could bring back one or two first-round picks.
Taylor Jenkins is the new Bucks coach. He is expected to push a pressure defense that forces turnovers and a faster transition game, and he may use a deep rotation.
Experts expect the Bucks to be a bad team and to make more trades to fix a roster that does not fit together.

durable.text: Strong shooter, solid defender and good passer.
Steals are his best category. He averages about 1.5 per game, well above the top 250 pool.
Best suited as a combo guard but good enough to be a primary point guard. His floor is a low-end NBA starter.

note: Rollins is one of the best value plays in the pool. He finished around 51st last season and experts see a top 50 player with top 40 upside, but auction averages are only 2.0 USD on Yahoo and 2.2 USD on ESPN, while Yahoo values him at 17 USD. No category is flagged weak, so he fits any build. He adds steals (1.4), assists (5.2) and threes (2.3), but at 2.5 per game turnovers are his weakest spot. Early in the season, check that he starts next to Herro ahead of Porter and plays about 30 minutes, and watch for trade news before the 2027-03-04 deadline.
